preview_text: Egypt advanced from Group G in second place with five points. Mohamed Salah scored against New Zealand in Round 2 and has been involved in five goals across four World Cup appearances, continuing his run as Africa's most productive player at the tournament. He carries a knee concern into this match.

Omar Marmoush leads Egypt in DFS ownership as the primary forward and has been the team's most dangerous attacking outlet in transition. Mohamed Salah serves as corner kick taker when fit and available.

Egypt held Iran to a 1-1 draw in their final group game after winning their previous two matches. Their defensive record of three goals conceded in three games is one of the better marks among African sides at this tournament.

Omar Marmoush leads Egypt in opto as the focal point of their attack and carries the highest ceiling in this matchup. Mohamed Hany provides a budget option at right back with consistent involvement in wide areas.

Australia advanced from Group D in second place after a stunning 2-0 opening win over Turkey, in which Nestory Irankunda became the youngest player to score for Australia at a World Cup in the 27th minute. Connor Metcalfe added a second goal from range to complete the upset.

Cristian Volpato, Connor Metcalfe, and Aiden O'Neill all served as corner kick takers throughout the group stage. Goalkeeper Patrick Beach made eight saves against Turkey in his competitive international debut, a record for any Australian goalkeeper in a World Cup match.

Australia held Paraguay to a goalless draw in their final group game to secure second place in Group D on head-to-head goal difference. They have kept two clean sheets in three matches and conceded only twice in the group stage.

Jordan Bos and Aziz Behich provide budget stacking options at fullback with consistent wide involvement, while Nestory Irankunda offers forward upside off his group stage goal as Australia's most dynamic attacking player.

Lionel Messi enters this match as the tournament's leading scorer with six goals, including a 80th-minute substitute appearance that produced his seventh consecutive World Cup game with a goal — a record in the history of the competition. Argentina topped Group J with nine points.

Rodrigo De Paul and Lionel Messi both served as corner kick takers in the group stage. Lautaro Martinez scored a penalty and leads Argentina in non-Messi attacking output, while Enzo Fernandez anchors the midfield alongside Alexis Mac Allister.

Argentina went unbeaten through the group stage, winning all three matches and scoring nine goals. In Round 3 against Jordan, Giovani Lo Celso opened with a curling free-kick in the 19th minute before Martinez converted a penalty in the 31st to take Argentina into halftime 2-0 up.

Lionel Messi is the single most important DFS asset on the slate with the highest opto on the board and six tournament goals. Lautaro Martinez offers a stacking option as the second forward with a penalty and consistent attacking involvement throughout the group stage.

Cape Verde made history by becoming the smallest nation ever to reach the World Cup knockout rounds, qualifying in their tournament debut with three draws. Josimar Vozinha has been the standout figure in goal, saving a last-minute penalty against Uruguay to preserve a 2-2 draw and keep their campaign alive.

Sidny Cabral and Jamiro Monteiro served as Cape Verde's corner kick takers throughout the group stage. Dailon Livramento operated as the primary forward and provided the attacking threat on the transition that defines Cape Verde's style.

Cape Verde drew all three group games — 0-0 against Spain, 2-2 against Uruguay, and 0-0 against Saudi Arabia — to finish second in Group H on tiebreakers. Their 2-2 draw with Uruguay featured a penalty save from Vozinha in added time that became the defining moment of their group stage campaign.

Josimar Vozinha leads Cape Verde in DFS upside as the goalkeeper hero of the tournament with a penalty save in the group stage and the highest clean sheet odds of any keeper on this slate given the opponent. Jamiro Monteiro provides a budget creative option with corner kick delivery.

Colombia topped Group K with seven points and dominated their final match against Portugal despite the goalless scoreline. Davinson Sanchez had a goal ruled out by the slimmest offside margin in stoppage time as Colombia registered 24 shots to Portugal's 13.

James Rodriguez and Jhon Arias both served as corner kick takers. Daniel Munoz scored the only goal in Colombia's Round 2 win over DR Congo in the 40th minute, while Luis Diaz has been the team's most dynamic wide attacker throughout the group stage.

Colombia's group stage produced the best attacking underlying numbers of any South American side, with the highest shot count and most expected goals created of the eight group winners. They have conceded just once in three matches.

Luis Diaz leads Colombia's DFS output as the most creative and direct wide attacker, while Daniel Munoz offers a goal-scoring fullback at a mid-range salary after his group stage winner against DR Congo. James Rodriguez provides corner kick exposure from midfield.

Ghana advanced as one of the best third-placed teams with four points after wins over Panama and a narrow 1-2 loss to Croatia in their final group game. Derrick Luckassen equalized in the Croatia match before Nikola Vlasic headed in a late winner from a Modric corner.

Jordan Ayew served as Ghana's primary corner kick taker. Thomas Partey anchors the midfield and has been influential in Ghana's defensive organization, which includes a disciplined low block structure that held England to a goalless draw in Round 2.

Ghana conceded only one goal in their first two group games, keeping England scoreless in a tactically disciplined 0-0 draw. Antoine Semenyo scored their opening goal of the tournament against Panama and carries a fitness concern entering the knockout round.

Jordan Ayew provides the best DFS value from Ghana as the primary forward and corner kick taker with consistent involvement across all three group games. Marvin Senaya at right back is the second-highest opto player from Ghana and offers a budget stack option.
